title: The Room of Vessel Farm
premise: Casper Winterbourne returns to the decaying family farmhouse to bury her twin sister Wren—except the body in the casket is wearing Casper's face, and no one else seems to notice. Twenty years ago, the twins made a bargain with something in the cellar called the Vessel Room: one of them would be 'counted' so the other could live. Casper fled and built a life on denial, but the house has kept her room exactly as she left it, and her sleep recordings now capture a second voice answering questions she never asked aloud. As she digs into her mother's ledgers, Casper learns the family survived generations by feeding the count a vessel every twenty years—and this time the debt is due at the equinox. To save her niece Ida from being taken, Casper must return to the Room of Vessel Farm and offer herself as the wrong twin, finally becoming the sibling who was buried.
about_author: Vesper Okafor is a former archivist of rural estate records who grew up in a farming family that never spoke of the relatives who 'went to town and didn't come back.' Their fiction excavates the quiet horrors hidden in inheritance, land, and family silence.

chapters.title: The Wrong Face in the Casket
chapters.summary: POV Casper. At the funeral home, Casper lifts the veil and finds her own face on the corpse everyone calls Wren. The funeral director insists it's grief playing tricks. Emotional beat: vertigo—the first crack in twenty years of careful denial.

chapters.title: Homecoming, Unchanged
chapters.summary: POV Casper. She moves into the farmhouse to settle the estate, finding her childhood bedroom preserved like a shrine—dust-free, bed turned down, waiting. Her brother-in-law Theo watches her too closely. Beat: dread dressed as hospitality.

chapters.title: Noises Have Explanations
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Night one: footsteps above a house with no second floor, a rhythmic counting under the floorboards. Casper catalogs rational explanations in her journal, the way she always has. Beat: the discipline of denial beginning to fail.

chapters.title: Ida Knows the Rules
chapters.summary: POV Ida, age nine. The niece shows Casper the household rules scrawled inside a cupboard: don't answer if your name is called twice, never count out loud past nine. Ida recites them like a bedtime prayer. Beat: chilling innocence; the child knows more than the adults admit.

chapters.title: The Recorder Under the Pillow
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Unable to trust her own memory, Casper sets an audio recorder while she sleeps. Playback captures her own voice asking questions she doesn't remember asking—and a second voice, low and patient, answering each one correctly. Beat: terror of being known.

chapters.title: What the Second Voice Says
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Night after night, the recordings accumulate. The voice answers questions about the farm's history with impossible accuracy, then begins asking its own: 'Is she ready? Is she willing?' Beat: surveillance inverted—Casper is the specimen.

chapters.title: Mother's Ledgers
chapters.summary: POV Casper. In the locked study, Casper finds her mother's meticulous ledgers: dates every twenty years, names crossed out, payments recorded in units of 'vessel.' The last entry, dated for this equinox, lists two candidates—I.W. and C.W. Beat: the horror of bookkeeping.

chapters.title: Theo's Silence
chapters.summary: POV Theo. He confesses he married into this knowing: his wife, Casper's late sister Mara, died refusing to name a vessel. He stayed to protect Ida but has been marking days off a calendar he can't explain. Beat: complicity and exhausted love.

chapters.title: The Cellar Door Is Warm
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Investigating the counting sound, Casper finds the cellar door warm as skin and breathing faintly. Scratched beside it: tally marks reaching nineteen. Beat: physical confrontation with the thing beneath denial.

chapters.title: Wren's Letters
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Hidden in the preserved bedroom, letters from Wren written after Casper fled—pleading, then bitter, then strange, describing how the house 'kept' her because a promised twin never came back. Beat: guilt sharpening into understanding.

chapters.title: The Bargain of 2004
chapters.summary: POV Casper, memory chapter. Flashback: sixteen-year-old twins in the Vessel Room, promised that only one would be counted. Casper ran; Wren stayed to hold the debt open. The face in the casket was the price of Casper's absence. Beat: devastating self-recognition.

chapters.title: Ida Starts Counting
chapters.summary: POV Ida. Ida begins sleepwalking, counting aloud toward ten, waking with dirt under her nails. Theo barricades her door; the marks on the cellar wall become twenty. Beat: the deadline made flesh—a child being prepared.

chapters.title: Running Was Never an Option
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper tries to take Ida and leave; the road loops back to the farm no matter which direction they drive. The radio plays her own recorded voice. Beat: claustrophobic despair—invisibility revoked, escape impossible.

chapters.title: The Second Voice Has a Name
chapters.summary: POV Casper. On the recording, the voice finally identifies itself: it is what remains of Wren, half-kept by the house since 2004, sustained only by answering. It warns: the count must be paid or it will choose Ida. Beat: horror braided with heartbreak.

chapters.title: Equinox Eve
chapters.summary: POV Theo. The household prepares without admitting it—salt at thresholds, mirrors covered, Ida dressed in white 'for church.' Theo begs Casper to flee alone; she refuses. Beat: doomed tenderness before the storm.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: POV Casper. At midnight the cellar opens itself. Casper descends into the Vessel Room: a chamber lined with niches, each holding a shape that might once have been a Winterbourne. Wren's voice guides her down. Beat: awe and dread fused.

chapters.title: The Count Reaches Ten
chapters.summary: POV Ida. Sleepwalking, Ida reaches the top of the stairs counting 'nine—' as the house pulls her toward the cellar. Theo holds her back, bleeding from where the doorframe bites him. Beat: climax igniting—the innocent nearly spent.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Debt
chapters.summary: POV Casper. In the Room, Casper confronts the counting presence and offers herself—not as Wren's substitute but as the twin who broke the bargain, claiming the debt as hers alone. The presence weighs her confession. Beat: moral climax; survival reframed as sacrifice.

chapters.title: Becoming the Buried Twin
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper steps into the empty niche wearing Wren's name, letting the house count her as the sister who stayed all along. The recordings' second voice goes silent mid-question. Beat: transcendent horror—identity surrendered willingly.

chapters.title: Morning After the Equinox
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Dawn: the cellar is cold stone, the tallies gone, Ida sleeping clean and ordinary. There is no record Casper ever arrived—only a second grave beside Wren's, already settled earth. Beat: hollow relief and grief.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: POV Ida, years later. Ida, grown, keeps her mother's and aunt's ledgers, adding nothing new. She visits the graves, leaves two flowers, and teaches no one the rules. Beat: bittersweet resolution—memory carried without repetition.

chapters.title: The Recording That Still Plays
chapters.summary: POV Ida. Packing the farmhouse for sale, Ida finds Casper's old recorder. One file remains: Casper's voice asking, 'Did it work?'—and after a long silence, a voice like both twins at once answers, softly, 'Ask me again tomorrow.' Final beat: the price of survival never fully paid.
